Package com.signalwire.sdk.datamap

Class DataMap

java.lang.Object
com.signalwire.sdk.datamap.DataMap
public class DataMap extends Object
Fluent builder for creating SWAIG data_map configurations.

DataMap tools execute on SignalWire servers without requiring webhook endpoints. Supports variable expansion: ${args.param}, ${response.field}, ${global_data.key}, ${foreach.item}.

All methods return this for fluent chaining.

    • getName

    • purpose

      public DataMap purpose(String description)
      Set the LLM-facing tool description — this is PROMPT ENGINEERING, not developer documentation.

      The description string is rendered into the OpenAI tool schema description field on every LLM turn. The model reads it to decide WHEN to call this tool. A vague purpose() is the #1 cause of "the model has the right tool but doesn't call it" failures with data-map tools.

      Bad vs good

      
 BAD : .purpose("weather api")
 GOOD: .purpose("Get the current weather conditions and forecast "
              + "for a specific city. Use this whenever the user "
              + "asks about weather, temperature, rain, or similar "
              + "conditions in a named location.")
      Parameters:
      description - prompt-engineering description of when to call this tool.

    • description

      public DataMap description(String description)
      Alias for purpose(String); sets the LLM-facing tool description. This string is read by the model to decide WHEN to call this tool. See purpose(String) for bad-vs-good examples.

    • parameter

      public DataMap parameter(String name, String paramType, String description, boolean required, List<String> enumValues)
      Add a parameter to this data-map tool — the description is LLM-FACING.

      Each parameter description is rendered into the OpenAI tool schema under parameters.properties.<name>.description and sent to the model. The model uses it to decide HOW to fill in the argument from user speech. It is prompt engineering, not developer FYI.

      Bad vs good

      
 BAD : .parameter("city", "string", "the city", true, null)
 GOOD: .parameter("city", "string",
           "The name of the city to get weather for, e.g. "
           + "\"San Francisco\". Ask the user if they did not "
           + "provide one. Include the state or country if the "
           + "city name is ambiguous.", true, null)
